title: Normal domain and normal ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. If $R$ is an integral domain, it is a *normal domain* if it is integrally closed in its field of fractions: every element of $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ that is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $R$ lies in $R$. The ring $R$ is a *normal ring* if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain.
